title: Fill time is not water saved
hook: A slower flow takes longer to fill the same bucket.

knows: that a model can declare hypothetical quantities
doesNotKnow: Distinguish fixed-volume filling from fixed-duration water use.

misconception: A slower flow necessarily uses less water to fill a fixed container.
objective: Distinguish fixed-volume filling from fixed-duration water use.

claims.text: A fixed 10L volume is filled by hypothetical constant flows of 5L/min or 2.5L/min. No spills occur. Scaled model; illustrative rates; fixed volume; no spills.
claims.source: Declared hypothetical inputs and limits in resource-specs.json. No actual product, price, tariff, shelf-life, treatment or physical appliance specification is asserted.

claims.text: The stage's two results are computed by the printed expressions. At Bucket=10L, A=2min and B=4min. Geometry follows the declared dimension relationships. Other pictures use a fixed full scale across the slider range; continuous fills and arcs show relative amounts rather than literal object counts.
claims.source: src/lib/lifehacks/resource-specs.json contains this lesson's numeric AST; src/lib/lifehacks/resource-model.ts evaluates it. A=["/","x",5]; B=["/","x",2.5]; x denotes Bucket. At x=10, A=2, B=4; recall at x=13: B=5.2. Values are fictional/ideal assumptions, not measurements. Display rounds to at most three decimals. Diagram scale: resourceGraphicScale in resource-model.ts takes the maximum modeled magnitude across both formulas and the declared slider range. For non-geometry figures, full-scale values are displayed; the scale stays fixed when the slider changes. Energy axis endpoints use resourceAxisEnd, including B=5×A hours in lh-watts-hours-trade; cylinder rx and ry both scale with radius in resourceCylinderDimensions.

claims.text: Divide the required volume by flow rate to get fill time. Both cases deliver the same bucket volume; the slower case only takes longer under these assumptions.
claims.source: src/lib/lifehacks/resource-specs.json contains this lesson's numeric AST; src/lib/lifehacks/resource-model.ts evaluates it. A=["/","x",5]; B=["/","x",2.5]; x denotes Bucket. At x=10, A=2, B=4; recall at x=13: B=5.2. Values are fictional/ideal assumptions, not measurements. Display rounds to at most three decimals. The principle follows from those expressions and stated scenario limits.

claims.text: A fixed 10L volume is filled by hypothetical constant flows of 5L/min or 2.5L/min. No spills occur. Change only Bucket to 13L. What is B (2.5L/min) now? Correct: 5.2min. Use B's stated rule with Bucket=13L: it gives 5.2min. Divide the required volume by flow rate to get fill time. Both cases deliver the same bucket volume; the slower case only takes longer under these assumptions.

recall.question: A fixed 10L volume is filled by hypothetical constant flows of 5L/min or 2.5L/min. No spills occur. Change only Bucket to 13L. What is B (2.5L/min) now?
recall.why: Use B's stated rule with Bucket=13L: it gives 5.2min. Divide the required volume by flow rate to get fill time. Both cases deliver the same bucket volume; the slower case only takes longer under these assumptions.

safety.assumptions: A fixed 10L volume is filled by hypothetical constant flows of 5L/min or 2.5L/min. No spills occur.
safety.excluded: No chemical mixtures, medical advice, wiring, safety-device bypass, actual tariffs, financial recommendations, temperature, food-storage or food-safety instructions. All energy powers, durations and tariffs are illustrative.
